title: Attempts, refusals, urges, permission, favours and pretence

constructions.label: Volitional + とする: attempt or be about to
て-form + みる: try and see
Volitional + としない: won't (make an effort to)
ない-form + ようにしている: make a point of not doing
て-form + ごらん: invite a junior listener to try
ずにはいられない: cannot help doing
なければならない: must (rule or need)
てもかまわない: it is all right to (do / not do)
てはいけない: must not
助言: たらいい／といい／ばいい recommend what would be good
許可: てもかまわない／てもいい allow an action
Causative + てもらう: be allowed to do; do (humbly)
て-form + もらう: have someone do

relationships.label: Attempted or about to happen, versus actually tried out
Observed unwillingness versus a chosen practice of not doing
Inviting the listener to try versus the speaker's own trial
An urge that cannot be held back versus an obligation
Advice about what would be good versus permission
No need to do versus must do
Who acts: the speaker with permission, or someone else for the speaker
A deliberately false appearance versus a genuine one

exercises.prompt: くつをはいて、家を____ら、電話が鳴って、出かけるのが遅くなった。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 出る（でる, leave; go out）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た); the ら after the blank is already printed. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: 出かけるのが遅くなった says the departure was delayed, so the speaker had not yet left when the phone rang.
exercises.explanation: I had put my shoes on and was just about to leave the house when the phone rang, so I was late going out. Volitional + としたら marks the moment just before an intended action, when something interrupts it.

options.label: 出てみた
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: て + みる says the action is actually done to see what it is like or what happens. Leaving is not being tested to see what happens, and 出かけるのが遅くなった says the speaker had not yet left when the phone rang.

options.label: 出ようとした
options.rationale: Fits: I had put my shoes on and was just about to leave the house when the phone rang, so I was late going out. Volitional + としたら marks the moment just before an intended action, when something interrupts it.

exercises.prompt: 赤ちゃんが今朝、いすにつかまって、一人で____。でも、まだ足が弱くて、立てない。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 立つ（たつ, stand up）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た or 〜ていた). Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: The next sentence, まだ…立てない, says the baby still cannot stand, so the standing did not happen.
exercises.explanation: This morning the baby held on to a chair and tried to stand up by itself. But its legs are still weak and it can't stand. Volitional + とした reports an effort without saying it succeeded.

options.label: 立ってみた
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: て + みる says the action is actually done to see what it is like or what happens. 立ってみた would mean the baby actually stood up to see what it was like, but the next sentence says it still cannot stand.

options.label: 立とうとした
options.rationale: Fits: This morning the baby held on to a chair and tried to stand up by itself. But its legs are still weak and it can't stand. Volitional + とした reports an effort without saying it succeeded.

exercises.prompt: 電車のドアが____とき、男の人が走って乗ってきた。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 閉まる（しまる, (a door) close）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た or 〜ていた). Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: The subject is a train door, which cannot try anything; the blank marks the moment it was about to close.
exercises.explanation: Just as the train doors were about to close, a man ran in and got on. With a subject that has no will, volitional + とした とき means 'was about to'.

options.label: 閉まってみた
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: て + みる says the action is actually done to see what it is like or what happens. A door has no intention, so it cannot do something to see what happens; the sentence marks the moment it was about to close.

options.label: 閉まろうとした
options.rationale: Fits: Just as the train doors were about to close, a man ran in and got on. With a subject that has no will, volitional + とした とき means 'was about to'.

exercises.prompt: 部屋に____が、かぎがかかっていて入れなかった。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 入る（はいる, enter）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た). Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: The continuation 入れなかった says the entering never happened.
exercises.explanation: I tried to go into the room, but it was locked and I couldn't get in. Volitional + としたが presents an attempt that failed.

options.label: 入ってみた
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: て + みる says the action is actually done to see what it is like or what happens. 'Went in as a trial' contradicts the following 入れなかった (could not get in).

options.label: 入ろうとした
options.rationale: Fits: I tried to go into the room, but it was locked and I couldn't get in. Volitional + としたが presents an attempt that failed.

exercises.prompt: 彼女は何か____が、結局、何も言わなかった。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 言う（いう, say）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た). Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: 結局、何も言わなかった says nothing was actually said.
exercises.explanation: She was about to say something, but in the end she said nothing. Volitional + としたが marks an action that was begun or intended but not carried out.

options.label: 言ってみた
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: て + みる says the action is actually done to see what it is like or what happens. 'Said something as a trial' contradicts 結局、何も言わなかった (in the end she said nothing).

options.label: 言おうとした
options.rationale: Fits: She was about to say something, but in the end she said nothing. Volitional + としたが marks an action that was begun or intended but not carried out.

exercises.prompt: 初めて納豆を____ら、思ったよりおいしかった。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 食べる（たべる, eat）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た); the ら after the blank is already printed. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: Finding out the taste (おいしかった) requires actually eating.
exercises.explanation: When I tried natto for the first time, it was tastier than I expected. て + みたら: the action is done to see what it is like, and the discovery follows.

options.label: 食べてみた
options.rationale: Fits: When I tried natto for the first time, it was tastier than I expected. て + みたら: the action is done to see what it is like, and the discovery follows.

options.label: 食べようとした
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: volitional + とした only says the action was set about or about to start, not that it was completed. The taste can only be discovered after eating, so being about to eat does not lead to おいしかった.

exercises.prompt: 友だちに勧められたアプリを一週間____が、思ったほど便利ではなかった。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 使う（つかう, use）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + とする frame or in the て-form + みる frame. Required form: plain past (〜た). Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: Using the app for a week (一週間) and judging that it was less convenient than expected both require actually using it.
exercises.explanation: I tried the app a friend recommended for a week, but it wasn't as convenient as I had expected. て + みたが presents a trial that was carried out, followed by a disappointing result.

options.label: 使ってみた
options.rationale: Fits: I tried the app a friend recommended for a week, but it wasn't as convenient as I had expected. て + みたが presents a trial that was carried out, followed by a disappointing result.

options.label: 使おうとした
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: volitional + とした only says the action was set about or about to start, not that it was completed. 一週間 and the verdict 思ったほど便利ではなかった both need real use; being about to use the app leads to neither.

exercises.prompt: 医者に何度言われても、父はたばこを____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: やめる（やめる, quit; stop）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + としない frame or in the ない-form + ようにしている frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: Despite repeated advice from the doctor, the father does not act: an observed refusal.
exercises.explanation: However many times the doctor tells him, my father won't (make any effort to) quit smoking. Volitional + としない describes someone's unwillingness to act.

options.label: やめようとしない
options.rationale: Fits: However many times the doctor tells him, my father won't (make any effort to) quit smoking. Volitional + としない describes someone's unwillingness to act.

options.label: やめないようにしている
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ないようにしている describes a practice the subject keeps up on purpose, usually for a reason of their own. Here it would mean the father keeps up a deliberate practice of not quitting, which makes no sense after the doctor's repeated advice.

exercises.prompt: 猫は具合が悪くなってから、水も____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 飲む（のむ, drink）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + としない frame or in the ない-form + ようにしている frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: A cat that has become ill shows no willingness to drink; nothing suggests a chosen practice.
exercises.explanation: Since the cat became ill, it won't even drink water. Volitional + としない describes an observed refusal, here by an animal.

options.label: 飲もうとしない
options.rationale: Fits: Since the cat became ill, it won't even drink water. Volitional + としない describes an observed refusal, here by an animal.

options.label: 飲まないようにしている
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ないようにしている describes a practice the subject keeps up on purpose, usually for a reason of their own. A sick cat does not keep up a deliberate plan of not drinking; the sentence reports its refusal.

exercises.prompt: 注射がこわくて、子どもはお母さんの後ろから____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 動く（うごく, move）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + としない frame or in the ない-form + ようにしている frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: Fear in one situation makes the child refuse to move: a momentary refusal, not a maintained practice.
exercises.explanation: Scared of the injection, the child won't move from behind its mother. Volitional + としない reports the refusal seen in this situation.

options.label: 動こうとしない
options.rationale: Fits: Scared of the injection, the child won't move from behind its mother. Volitional + としない reports the refusal seen in this situation.

options.label: 動かないようにしている
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ないようにしている describes a practice the subject keeps up on purpose, usually for a reason of their own. Fear of one injection causes a refusal now; it is not a habit the child keeps up for a reason.

exercises.prompt: 眠れなくなるので、夜はできるだけコーヒーを____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 飲む（のむ, drink）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + としない frame or in the ない-form + ようにしている frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: できるだけ and a reason of one's own (not being able to sleep) point to a deliberate practice.
exercises.explanation: Because it keeps me awake, I try not to drink coffee in the evening as far as possible. ないようにしている describes a practice one keeps up on purpose.
acceptedAnswers: 飲まないようにしている
のまないようにしている
飲まないようにしてる
のまないようにしてる

options.label: 飲もうとしない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: volitional + としない reports someone's observed unwillingness to act. Combined with できるだけ and the speaker's own reason, an outside report of unwillingness does not fit; the sentence describes a habit the speaker maintains.

options.label: 飲まないようにしている
options.rationale: Fits: Because it keeps me awake, I try not to drink coffee in the evening as far as possible. ないようにしている describes a practice one keeps up on purpose.

exercises.prompt: 〔いつも階段を使う理由を聞かれて〕足を強くしたいから、エスカレーターは____んだ。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 使う（つかう, use）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the volitional + としない frame or in the ない-form + ようにしている frame. Required form: plain nonpast; the んだ after the blank is already printed. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: Asked about a habit (いつも階段), the speaker explains a practice of their own with its purpose.
exercises.explanation: (Asked why they always take the stairs) I want to strengthen my legs, so I make a point of not using escalators. ないようにしている states one's own deliberate practice, here explained with んだ.
acceptedAnswers: 使わないようにしている
つかわないようにしている
使わないようにしてる
つかわないようにしてる

options.label: 使おうとしない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: volitional + としない reports someone's observed unwillingness to act. The speaker is explaining a habit of their own that someone noticed; volitional + としない is an outside report of someone's unwillingness and does not describe one's own chosen practice.

options.label: 使わないようにしている
options.rationale: Fits: (Asked why they always take the stairs) I want to strengthen my legs, so I make a point of not using escalators. ないようにしている states one's own deliberate practice, here explained with んだ.

exercises.prompt: 〔父が子どもに〕ほら、この穴から____。小さい鳥がいるよ。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: のぞく（のぞく, peek; look into）. Fill the blank with this verb in its て-form followed either by ごらん or by plain nonpast みる. ご覧／御覧 and ごらんなさい are also accepted spellings of the first frame.
exercises.evidence: ほら and the following よ-information are aimed at the child: the father wants the child to look.
exercises.explanation: (Father to child) Look, peek through this hole. There's a little bird in there. Vてごらん invites a junior listener to try something and see.
acceptedAnswers: のぞいてごらんなさい

options.label: のぞいてみる
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: with a full stop, plain みる announces the speaker's own trial. The father already knows what is inside and tells the child (いるよ), so he is inviting the child to look.

options.label: のぞいてごらん
options.rationale: Fits: (Father to child) Look, peek through this hole. There's a little bird in there. Vてごらん invites a junior listener to try something and see.

exercises.prompt: 〔先生が生徒に〕ゆうきくん、失敗してもいいから、もう一度自分で____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: やる（やる, do）. Fill the blank with this verb in its て-form followed either by ごらん or by plain nonpast みる. ご覧／御覧 and ごらんなさい are also accepted spellings of the first frame.
exercises.evidence: The teacher addresses Yuuki by name and tells him he may fail: the trying is Yuuki's.
exercises.explanation: (Teacher to pupil) Yuuki, it's fine if you fail, so try doing it once more by yourself. Vてごらん is a gentle instruction from a senior to try something.

options.label: やってみる
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: with a full stop, plain みる announces the speaker's own trial. The teacher addresses ゆうきくん and says it is fine to fail, so the trying belongs to the pupil, not the teacher.

options.label: やってごらん
options.rationale: Fits: (Teacher to pupil) Yuuki, it's fine if you fail, so try doing it once more by yourself. Vてごらん is a gentle instruction from a senior to try something.

exercises.prompt: 〔祖母が孫に〕このりんご、とても甘いから、一口____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 食べる（たべる, eat）. Fill the blank with this verb in its て-form followed either by ごらん or by plain nonpast みる. ご覧／御覧 and ごらんなさい are also accepted spellings of the first frame.
exercises.evidence: The grandmother already knows the apple is sweet and offers the grandchild a bite.
exercises.explanation: (Grandmother to grandchild) This apple is really sweet, so have a bite and see. Vてごらん invites the listener to try.

options.label: 食べてみる
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: with a full stop, plain みる announces the speaker's own trial. The grandmother already knows it is sweet; she is offering the grandchild a taste.

options.label: 食べてごらん
options.rationale: Fits: (Grandmother to grandchild) This apple is really sweet, so have a bite and see. Vてごらん invites the listener to try.

exercises.prompt: 〔母が子どもに〕この貝を耳に当てて____。海の音が聞こえるよ。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 聞く（きく, listen）. Fill the blank with this verb in its て-form followed either by ごらん or by plain nonpast みる. ご覧／御覧 and ごらんなさい are also accepted spellings of the first frame.
exercises.evidence: The mother tells the child what it will hear (聞こえるよ): she is inviting the child to listen.
exercises.explanation: (Mother to child) Hold this shell to your ear and listen. You can hear the sea. Vてごらん invites a junior listener to try something and discover the result.

options.label: 聞いてみる
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: with a full stop, plain みる announces the speaker's own trial. The よ-sentence tells the child what they will hear, so the mother is inviting the child to listen.

options.label: 聞いてごらん
options.rationale: Fits: (Mother to child) Hold this shell to your ear and listen. You can hear the sea. Vてごらん invites a junior listener to try something and discover the result.

exercises.prompt: 〔子どもが父に〕本当？じゃあ、ぼくもその穴から____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: のぞく（のぞく, peek; look into）. Fill the blank with this verb in its て-form followed either by ごらん or by plain nonpast みる. ご覧／御覧 and ごらんなさい are also accepted spellings of the first frame.
exercises.evidence: ぼくも makes the child, the speaker, the one who will look.
exercises.explanation: (Child to father) Really? Then I'll peek through that hole too. Plain みる after the て-form announces the speaker's own trial.

options.label: のぞいてみる
options.rationale: Fits: (Child to father) Really? Then I'll peek through that hole too. Plain みる after the て-form announces the speaker's own trial.

options.label: のぞいてごらん
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ごらん invites the listener to try something; it is never used for the speaker's own action. Here the child (ぼくも) is the one who will look.

exercises.prompt: 〔孫が台所で一人で〕祖母がくれたりんご、おいしそう。一口____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 食べる（たべる, eat）. Fill the blank with this verb in its て-form followed either by ごらん or by plain nonpast みる. ご覧／御覧 and ごらんなさい are also accepted spellings of the first frame.
exercises.evidence: The grandchild is alone and talking to themself, so there is no listener to invite; the trial is the speaker's own.
exercises.explanation: (The grandchild, alone in the kitchen) The apple Grandma gave me looks tasty. I'll have a bite. て-form + みる states the speaker's own trial, here as a nonpast 'I'll try'.

options.label: 食べてみる
options.rationale: Fits: (The grandchild, alone in the kitchen) The apple Grandma gave me looks tasty. I'll have a bite. て-form + みる states the speaker's own trial, here as a nonpast 'I'll try'.

options.label: 食べてごらん
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ごらん invites the listener to try something; it is never used for the speaker's own action. The grandchild is alone in the kitchen, so there is nobody to invite; ごらん always addresses a listener.

exercises.prompt: 友だちの話がとてもおかしくて、____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 笑う（わらう, laugh）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the ず + にはいられない frame or in the なければ + ならない frame. Required form: plain past (〜た). Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: The cause is a feeling (the story was very funny), not a rule.
exercises.explanation: My friend's story was so funny that I couldn't help laughing. ずにはいられない: a feeling makes holding back impossible. ないではいられない is a less common variant and is also accepted.
acceptedAnswers: 笑わずにはいられなかった
わらわずにはいられなかった
笑わないではいられなかった
わらわないではいられなかった

options.label: 笑わなければならなかった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: なければならない presents the action as required by a rule, duty or need. Funniness does not create a duty to laugh; it creates an urge that cannot be held back.

options.label: 笑わずにはいられなかった
options.rationale: Fits: My friend's story was so funny that I couldn't help laughing. ずにはいられない: a feeling makes holding back impossible. ないではいられない is a less common variant and is also accepted.

exercises.prompt: 娘が連絡もしないで夜遅くまで帰ってこないと、____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 心配する（しんぱいする, worry）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the ず + にはいられない frame or in the なければ + ならない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: Whenever the daughter stays out late without a word, a feeling arises that the parent cannot stop.
exercises.explanation: When my daughter doesn't come home until late at night without even getting in touch, I can't help worrying. ずにはいられない describes an unavoidable feeling. The irregular する becomes せず (not しず).
acceptedAnswers: 心配せずにはいられない
しんぱいせずにはいられない
心配しないではいられない
しんぱいしないではいられない

options.label: 心配しなければならない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: なければならない presents the action as required by a rule, duty or need. Worrying is not a requirement here; the と-clause describes a situation that triggers a feeling.

options.label: 心配せずにはいられない
options.rationale: Fits: When my daughter doesn't come home until late at night without even getting in touch, I can't help worrying. ずにはいられない describes an unavoidable feeling. The irregular する becomes せず (not しず).

exercises.prompt: 父は人の間違いを見つけると、一言____性格だ。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 言う（いう, say）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the ず + にはいられない frame or in the なければ + ならない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: 性格 (personality) points to an inner tendency, not to a rule.
exercises.explanation: My father has the kind of personality that can't help saying something whenever he finds someone's mistake. ずにはいられない describes an inner urge that keeps showing.
acceptedAnswers: 言わずにはいられない
いわずにはいられない
言わないではいられない
いわないではいられない

options.label: 言わなければならない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: なければならない presents the action as required by a rule, duty or need. The sentence describes his personality, an urge from inside; nothing requires him to comment.

options.label: 言わずにはいられない
options.rationale: Fits: My father has the kind of personality that can't help saying something whenever he finds someone's mistake. ずにはいられない describes an inner urge that keeps showing.

exercises.prompt: その小説はおもしろくて、一度読み始めると、最後まで____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 読む（よむ, read）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the ず + にはいられない frame or in the なければ + ならない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: The reason is that the novel is interesting: an urge to keep going.
exercises.explanation: That novel is so interesting that once you start reading it, you can't help reading to the end. ずにはいられない: interest makes stopping impossible.
acceptedAnswers: 読まずにはいられない
よまずにはいられない
読まないではいられない
よまないではいられない

options.label: 読まなければならない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: なければならない presents the action as required by a rule, duty or need. No assignment or rule is mentioned; the novel's appeal makes it impossible to stop reading.

options.label: 読まずにはいられない
options.rationale: Fits: That novel is so interesting that once you start reading it, you can't help reading to the end. ずにはいられない: interest makes stopping impossible.

exercises.prompt: 会社の規則で、報告書は毎週金曜日までに____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 出す（だす, hand in; submit）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the ず + にはいられない frame or in the なければ + ならない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: 会社の規則で gives an outside rule as the source.
exercises.explanation: Under company rules, reports must be handed in by Friday every week. なければならない states an obligation; other must-forms such as なければいけない and ないといけない are also accepted.
acceptedAnswers: 出さなければならない
出さなければいけない
出さなくてはならない
出さなくてはいけない
ださなければならない
ださなければいけない
ださなくてはならない
ださなくてはいけない

options.label: 出さなければならない
options.rationale: Fits: Under company rules, reports must be handed in by Friday every week. なければならない states an obligation; other must-forms such as なければいけない and ないといけない are also accepted.

options.label: 出さずにはいられない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ずにはいられない says an inner feeling makes it impossible to hold back. A company rule creates an obligation; it is not a feeling that makes the writer unable to hold back.

exercises.prompt: 医者に言われたので、この薬は毎朝____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 飲む（のむ, take (medicine); drink）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the ず + にはいられない frame or in the なければ + ならない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. Type the verb and its ending as one string.
exercises.evidence: The doctor's instruction is an outside requirement.
exercises.explanation: Because the doctor told me to, I have to take this medicine every morning. なければならない presents the action as required; other must-forms are also accepted.
acceptedAnswers: 飲まなければならない
飲まなければいけない
飲まなくてはならない
飲まなくてはいけない
のまなければならない
のまなければいけない
のまなくてはならない
のまなくてはいけない

options.label: 飲まなければならない
options.rationale: Fits: Because the doctor told me to, I have to take this medicine every morning. なければならない presents the action as required; other must-forms are also accepted.

options.label: 飲まずにはいられない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ずにはいられない says an inner feeling makes it impossible to hold back. Taking medicine because a doctor said so is a requirement, not an urge that cannot be resisted.

exercises.prompt: この試験では、辞書を____。でも、スマホは使えません。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 使う（つかう, use）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the て-form + もかまわない frame (its negative なくても + かまわない is part of the same frame) or in the て-form + はいけない frame. Required form: polite nonpast (〜ません). 構わない is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: でも … スマホは使えません contrasts the phone with the dictionary, so the dictionary is allowed.
exercises.explanation: In this exam you may use a dictionary. Smartphones, however, cannot be used. てもかまいません gives permission.
acceptedAnswers: 使ってもかまいません
つかってもかまいません
つかっても構いません

options.label: 使ってもかまいません
options.rationale: Fits: In this exam you may use a dictionary. Smartphones, however, cannot be used. てもかまいません gives permission.

options.label: 使ってはいけません
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: てはいけない forbids the action. でも introduces the smartphone as the exception, which only makes sense if the dictionary is allowed.

exercises.prompt: 私は今日は時間があるから、あなたの仕事が終わるまで____よ。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 待つ（まつ, wait）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the て-form + もかまわない frame (its negative なくても + かまわない is part of the same frame) or in the て-form + はいけない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. 構わない is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The speaker has time today, so waiting is offered as acceptable to them: 'I don't mind'.
exercises.explanation: I have time today, so I don't mind waiting until your work is finished. てもかまわない can state that the speaker does not mind doing something.

options.label: 待ってもかまわない
options.rationale: Fits: I have time today, so I don't mind waiting until your work is finished. てもかまわない can state that the speaker does not mind doing something.

options.label: 待ってはいけない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: てはいけない forbids the action. Having free time is a reason the speaker can wait, not a reason waiting would be forbidden.

exercises.prompt: 明日の練習は自由参加です。用事がある人は____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 来る（くる, come）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the なくても + かまわない frame or in the なければ + いけない frame. Required form: polite nonpast (〜ません). 構わない is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: 自由参加 (optional attendance) means nobody is required to come.
exercises.explanation: Tomorrow's practice is optional. People who have something to do don't have to come. なくてもかまいません says that not doing the action is acceptable.
acceptedAnswers: 来なくてもかまいません
来なくても構いません
こなくてもかまいません
こなくても構いません

options.label: 来なければいけません
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: なければいけない makes coming a requirement, but 自由参加 means attendance is optional.

options.label: 来なくてもかまいません
options.rationale: Fits: 自由参加 means not coming is acceptable.

exercises.prompt: 明日の練習で試合に出るメンバーを決めます。試合に出たい人は____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 来る（くる, come）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the なくても + かまわない frame or in the なければ + いけない frame. Required form: polite nonpast (〜ません). 構わない is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The team is chosen at tomorrow's practice, so anyone who wants to play needs to be there.
exercises.explanation: The members who will play in the match are chosen at tomorrow's practice. Anyone who wants to play has to come. なければいけない presents the action as needed; other must-forms are also accepted.
acceptedAnswers: 来なければいけません
来なければなりません
来なくてはいけません
来なくてはなりません
こなければいけません
こなければなりません
こなくてはいけません
こなくてはなりません

options.label: 来なければいけません
options.rationale: Fits: the team is chosen at this practice, so coming is necessary for anyone who wants to play.

options.label: 来なくてもかまいません
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: なくてもかまわない says not coming is fine, but players are chosen at this practice, so anyone who wants to play cannot stay away.

exercises.prompt: この美術館の中では、作品の写真を____。カメラはロッカーに入れてください。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 撮る（とる, take (a photo)）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the て-form + もかまわない frame (its negative なくても + かまわない is part of the same frame) or in the て-form + はいけない frame. Required form: polite nonpast (〜ません). 構わない is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: Cameras must go into a locker, so photography is not allowed.
exercises.explanation: Inside this museum you must not take photos of the works. Please put cameras in a locker. てはいけません forbids an action.

options.label: 撮ってもかまいません
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: てもかまわない says the action is allowed or acceptable. Asking visitors to lock their cameras away would make no sense if photos were allowed.

options.label: 撮ってはいけません
options.rationale: Fits: Inside this museum you must not take photos of the works. Please put cameras in a locker. てはいけません forbids an action.

exercises.prompt: この川は流れが速くて危ないから、ここで____よ。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 泳ぐ（およぐ, swim）. Fill the blank with this verb either in the て-form + もかまわない frame (its negative なくても + かまわない is part of the same frame) or in the て-form + はいけない frame. Required form: plain nonpast. 構わない is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The river is dangerous: a reason to forbid swimming.
exercises.explanation: The current in this river is fast and dangerous, so you mustn't swim here. てはいけない forbids an action.

options.label: 泳いでもかまわない
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: てもかまわない says the action is allowed or acceptable. Danger is a reason to forbid swimming, not to allow it.

options.label: 泳いではいけない
options.rationale: Fits: The current in this river is fast and dangerous, so you mustn't swim here. てはいけない forbids an action.

exercises.prompt:
「駅前のホテルまで、どうやって行けばいいですか。」
話し手が求めているのは____だ。
exercises.translation: Read the quoted remark and complete the second line with one label: 助言（じょげん, advice: what would be good to do） or 許可（きょか, permission: the action is allowed）.
exercises.evidence: どうやって … ばいいですか asks what would be the best way to act.
exercises.explanation: "How should I get to the hotel in front of the station?" The speaker is asking for advice. ばいいですか, like たらいいですか, asks what would be a good thing to do.

options.label: 助言
options.rationale: Fits: "How should I get to the hotel in front of the station?" The speaker is asking for advice. ばいいですか, like たらいいですか, asks what would be a good thing to do.

options.label: 許可
options.rationale: Does not fit this remark: The question asks which way would be best, not whether going is allowed (that would be てもかまいませんか or てもいいですか).

spans.gloss: area in front of the station

exercises.prompt:
「疲れているなら、今日は早く寝るといいよ。」
話し手が与えているのは____だ。
exercises.translation: Read the quoted remark and complete the second line with one label: 助言（じょげん, advice: what would be good to do） or 許可（きょか, permission: the action is allowed）.
exercises.evidence: Vるといいよ recommends an action as a good idea.
exercises.explanation: "If you're tired, you should go to bed early today." The speaker is giving advice. といい, like たらいい, recommends what would be good to do.

options.label: 助言
options.rationale: Fits: "If you're tired, you should go to bed early today." The speaker is giving advice. といい, like たらいい, recommends what would be good to do.

options.label: 許可
options.rationale: Does not fit this remark: といいよ recommends going to bed as a good idea; it is not presented as something the listener is merely allowed to do.

exercises.prompt:
「この部屋で少し待ってもかまいませんか。」
話し手が求めているのは____だ。
exercises.translation: Read the quoted remark and complete the second line with one label: 助言（じょげん, advice: what would be good to do） or 許可（きょか, permission: the action is allowed）.
exercises.evidence: てもかまいませんか asks whether an action is acceptable.
exercises.explanation: "Would it be all right if I waited in this room for a while?" The speaker is asking for permission.

options.label: 助言
options.rationale: Does not fit this remark: The speaker already knows what to do (wait here) and asks whether it is acceptable, not what would be best.

options.label: 許可
options.rationale: Fits: "Would it be all right if I waited in this room for a while?" The speaker is asking for permission.

exercises.prompt:
〔店長がアルバイトに〕「明日、用事があるなら、休んでもいいよ。」
店長が与えているのは____だ。
exercises.translation: Read the quoted remark and complete the second line with one label: 助言（じょげん, advice: what would be good to do） or 許可（きょか, permission: the action is allowed）.
exercises.evidence: A manager says taking the day off is acceptable: permission from the person in charge.
exercises.explanation: (Manager to part-timer) "If you have something to do tomorrow, it's fine for you to take the day off." The manager is giving permission. てもいい, like てもかまわない, says an action is allowed.

options.label: 助言
options.rationale: Does not fit this remark: てもいいよ says the day off is allowed; the manager is not recommending a day off as the best course.

options.label: 許可
options.rationale: Fits: (Manager to part-timer) "If you have something to do tomorrow, it's fine for you to take the day off." The manager is giving permission. てもいい, like てもかまわない, says an action is allowed.

exercises.prompt: 熱があったので、店長に頼んで、昨日はアルバイトを____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 休む（やすむ, take time off; rest）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: plain past (〜た). 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The speaker had a fever and asked the manager: the speaker is the one who stays away.
exercises.explanation: I had a fever, so I asked the manager and was allowed to take yesterday off from my part-time job. Causative + てもらう: the speaker does the action with someone's permission.

options.label: 休んでもらった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: plain て-form + もらう means someone else does the action for the speaker. It would mean the manager took the day off for the speaker, but it is the speaker who had a fever.

options.label: 休ませてもらった
options.rationale: Fits: I had a fever, so I asked the manager and was allowed to take yesterday off from my part-time job. Causative + てもらう: the speaker does the action with someone's permission.

exercises.prompt: 自分のパソコンが壊れたので、兄のパソコンを少し____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 使う（つかう, use）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: plain past (〜た). 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The speaker's own computer broke, so the speaker is the one who uses the brother's.
exercises.explanation: My own computer broke, so my older brother let me use his for a while. Causative + てもらう: the speaker uses something with the owner's permission.

options.label: 使ってもらった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: plain て-form + もらう means someone else does the action for the speaker. It would mean the brother used his own computer for the speaker, but the speaker is the one who needs a computer.

options.label: 使わせてもらった
options.rationale: Fits: My own computer broke, so my older brother let me use his for a while. Causative + てもらう: the speaker uses something with the owner's permission.

exercises.prompt: 部長にお願いして、今日の会議では私が自分で新しい案を____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 発表する（はっぴょうする, present）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: plain past (〜た). 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: 私が自分で makes the speaker the presenter; the manager gave permission.
exercises.explanation: I asked the department manager, and at today's meeting I was allowed to present the new proposal myself. With する verbs the causative is させる: 発表させてもらった.
acceptedAnswers: はっぴょうさせてもらった
はっぴょうさせて貰った

options.label: 発表してもらった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: plain て-form + もらう means someone else does the action for the speaker. It would make someone else the presenter, which clashes with 私が自分で (I myself).

options.label: 発表させてもらった
options.rationale: Fits: I asked the department manager, and at today's meeting I was allowed to present the new proposal myself. With する verbs the causative is させる: 発表させてもらった.

exercises.prompt: すみません、気分が悪いので、今日は少し早く____か。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 帰る（かえる, go home）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: polite potential negative of もらう (〜もらえません), used as a request; the か after the blank is already printed. 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The speaker feels sick and asks to leave: the speaker is the one going home.
exercises.explanation: Excuse me, I'm not feeling well; could I go home a little early today? Causative + てもらえませんか asks for permission to do something oneself. 帰る is a godan verb: 帰らせる.
acceptedAnswers: 帰らせてもらえません
かえらせてもらえません
かえらせて貰えません

options.label: 帰ってもらえません
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: plain て-form + もらう means someone else does the action for the speaker. It would ask the listener to go home, but it is the speaker who feels sick.

options.label: 帰らせてもらえません
options.rationale: Fits: Excuse me, I'm not feeling well; could I go home a little early today? Causative + てもらえませんか asks for permission to do something oneself. 帰る is a godan verb: 帰らせる.

exercises.prompt: 〔会議で〕では、私から一言、意見を____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 言う（いう, say）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: polite nonpast (〜ます). 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: 私から (from me) makes the speaker the one who is about to state an opinion.
exercises.explanation: (At a meeting) Well then, allow me to say a word and give my opinion. Causative + てもらいます is a polite, modest way of announcing one's own action.

options.label: 言ってもらいます
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: plain て-form + もらう means someone else does the action for the speaker. It would mean someone else will do the saying, which clashes with 私から (from me).

options.label: 言わせてもらいます
options.rationale: Fits: (At a meeting) Well then, allow me to say a word and give my opinion. Causative + てもらいます is a polite, modest way of announcing one's own action.

exercises.prompt: 自分では直せないので、壊れた自転車を近所の自転車屋さんに____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 直す（なおす, repair）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: plain past (〜た). 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: 自分では直せない: the speaker cannot repair it, so someone else does.
exercises.explanation: I can't fix it myself, so I had the broken bicycle repaired at the local bike shop. Plain て-form + もらう: someone else does the action for the speaker.

options.label: 直してもらった
options.rationale: Fits: I can't fix it myself, so I had the broken bicycle repaired at the local bike shop. Plain て-form + もらう: someone else does the action for the speaker.

options.label: 直させてもらった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: causative + てもらう means the speaker does the action with someone's permission. It would mean the shop let the speaker do the repair, which contradicts 自分では直せない (cannot fix it myself).

exercises.prompt: この町に来たばかりのころ、近所の人に____パン屋に、今もよく行っている。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 教える（おしえる, tell; teach）. Fill the blank with this verb followed by a form of もらう, either as causative + てもらう or as plain て-form + もらう. Required form: plain past (〜た), modifying the noun パン屋. 貰う is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: A newcomer (来たばかりのころ) learns about a bakery from a neighbour: the neighbour is the one who told.
exercises.explanation: I still often go to the bakery a neighbour told me about when I had just moved to this town. Plain て-form + もらう, here modifying パン屋: the neighbour did the telling for the speaker.

options.label: 教えてもらった
options.rationale: Fits: I still often go to the bakery a neighbour told me about when I had just moved to this town. Plain て-form + もらう, here modifying パン屋: the neighbour did the telling for the speaker.

options.label: 教えさせてもらった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: causative + てもらう means the speaker does the action with someone's permission. It would mean the neighbour let the speaker do the telling, but a newcomer to the town is the one who needed to be told about a bakery.

exercises.prompt: 兄は答えを知っていたのに、わざと____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 知る（しる, know）. Fill the blank with this word in a predicate ending either in ふり + をする or in ようだ. Required form: plain negative of the verb before the ending; the ending in plain past (〜た or 〜ていた). 振り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: わざと (on purpose) plus the fact that he knew marks a deliberate act.
exercises.explanation: My older brother knew the answer, but he deliberately pretended not to know. ふりをする: a deliberately false appearance.
acceptedAnswers: 知らないふりをしていた
しらないふりをしていた
知らない振りをしていた
しらない振りをしていた

options.label: 知らないふりをした
options.rationale: Fits: My older brother knew the answer, but he deliberately pretended not to know. ふりをする: a deliberately false appearance.

options.label: 知らないようだった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ようだった reports how things genuinely appeared. わざと (on purpose) describes a deliberate act, and the sentence says he did know; a genuine appearance of not knowing does not fit.

exercises.prompt: 母は家族を心配させないように、病気なのに____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 元気（げんき, healthy; well (な-adjective)）. Fill the blank with this word in a predicate ending either in ふり + をする or in ようだ. Required form: the な-adjective form before the ending; the ending in the past (〜た or 〜ていた). 振り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: A purpose (so as not to worry the family) and 病気なのに show a deliberately false appearance.
exercises.explanation: So as not to worry the family, my mother acted as if she were well even though she was ill. A な-adjective takes な before ふり.
acceptedAnswers: 元気なふりをしていた
げんきなふりをしていた
元気な振りをしていた
げんきな振りをしていた

options.label: 元気なふりをしていた
options.rationale: Fits: So as not to worry the family, my mother acted as if she were well even though she was ill. A な-adjective takes な before ふり.

options.label: 元気なようだった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ようだった reports how things genuinely appeared. The purpose clause ように (so as not to worry the family) needs a deliberate action, and she was in fact ill.

exercises.prompt: 宿題をしたくなかったので、弟はソファーで____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 寝る（ねる, sleep）. Fill the blank with this word in a predicate ending either in ふり + をする or in ようだ. Required form: ている form of the verb before the ending; the ending in plain past (〜た or 〜ていた). 振り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: His motive (not wanting to do homework) makes the sleeping a cover, not a real state.
exercises.explanation: My younger brother didn't want to do his homework, so he pretended to be asleep on the sofa. Vている + ふりをする pretends to be in a state.
acceptedAnswers: 寝ているふりをしていた
ねているふりをしていた
寝ている振りをしていた
ねている振りをしていた

options.label: 寝ているふりをした
options.rationale: Fits: My younger brother didn't want to do his homework, so he pretended to be asleep on the sofa. Vている + ふりをする pretends to be in a state.

options.label: 寝ているようだった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ようだった reports how things genuinely appeared. The ので-clause gives his motive for acting, which points to a deliberate pretence rather than a genuine appearance.

exercises.prompt: 先生に聞かれて、まだ読んでいない本を____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 読む（よむ, read）. Fill the blank with this word in a predicate ending either in ふり + をする or in ようだ. Required form: plain past of the verb before the ending; the ending in plain past (〜た). 振り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: The book has not been read, yet the speaker gives the teacher the impression of having read it.
exercises.explanation: When the teacher asked, I pretended to have read a book I hadn't read yet. Vた + ふりをする pretends that something already happened.

options.label: 読んだふりをした
options.rationale: Fits: When the teacher asked, I pretended to have read a book I hadn't read yet. Vた + ふりをする pretends that something already happened.

options.label: 読んだようだった
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ようだった reports how things genuinely appeared. The speaker knows they have not read it, so a guess about their own reading makes no sense; the speaker is faking it.

exercises.prompt: 弟はヘッドホンで音楽を聞いていて、私が何度呼んでも____。肩をたたくと、びっくりした顔をした。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 聞こえる（きこえる, can hear; be audible）. Fill the blank with this word in a predicate ending either in ふり + をする or in ようだ. Required form: plain negative of the verb before the ending; the ending in plain past (〜た). 振り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: Headphones explain why he could not hear, and his startled face shows he truly had not noticed.
exercises.explanation: My younger brother was listening to music on headphones and, however many times I called, he didn't seem to hear me. When I tapped his shoulder, he looked startled. ようだった reports a genuine appearance.
acceptedAnswers: 聞こえないようだった
きこえないようだった
聞こえないみたいだった
きこえないみたいだった

options.label: 聞こえないふりをした
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ふりをする means deliberately putting on a false appearance. The headphones give a real reason he could not hear, and his surprise when tapped shows he had not noticed.

options.label: 聞こえないようだった
options.rationale: Fits: My younger brother was listening to music on headphones and, however many times I called, he didn't seem to hear me. When I tapped his shoulder, he looked startled. ようだった reports a genuine appearance.

exercises.prompt: 田中さんは今日、顔色が悪くて、とても____。
exercises.translation: Supplied word: 疲れる（つかれる, get tired）. Fill the blank with this word in a predicate ending either in ふり + をする or in ようだ. Required form: ている form of the verb before the ending; the ending in plain past (〜た). 振り is also accepted.
exercises.evidence: A pale complexion is outward evidence of a real state, not something one puts on.
exercises.explanation: Tanaka looked pale today and seemed very tired. ようだった draws a conclusion from what one observes.

options.label: 疲れているふりをした
options.rationale: Does not fit this context: ふりをする means deliberately putting on a false appearance. A pale complexion is evidence of a real condition; nothing suggests Tanaka was faking.

options.label: 疲れているようだった
options.rationale: Fits: Tanaka looked pale today and seemed very tired. ようだった draws a conclusion from what one observes.
